subject: Private/VPC pricing: token volumes, licensing, and environments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Private/VPC pricing discovery - next steps

Sanjay - thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the asks we committed to: 

- Summary of what we heard: PaymentsAI wants a Private (VPC) deployment for a customer-facing payments assistant. Key constraints: PII data stays in your VPC, needs SOC2-compliant controls, and multi-environment isolation (staging + prod, potentially a sandbox).
- Usage signals: you mentioned 1M monthly active users, ~150 tokens per session average, and 2x peak on promo days (confirm below).
- Commercial asks we took away: target $/1M tokens, approximate monthly token volume, and expected number of separate environments per deployment (e.g., 2 or 3) so we can price licensing + support.

Attachments: 20270624-redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (PDF, 120KB) - draft price ranges for Private/VPC options.

Please confirm the numbers below and drop any procurement contacts. Once we lock volumes and env counts I'll follow up with a private pricing proposal (license + per-1M token tranche + support tier).

Ask for you now: can you confirm the expected steady-state monthly tokens and peak-day multiplier (1.5x/2x)? Also who should I include from procurement to start SOW/PO discussions?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paymentsai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@paymentsai.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing discovery - next steps

Ben - good call, thanks. Confirming numbers from our side: 

- Steady-state monthly MAUs: ~1.0M (we're measuring MAU; sessions roughly equal to MAU with ~1.2 sessions/user/month).
- Tokens: from our telemetry the current average is ~150 tokens/session; target is to keep under heavier prompts. That gives ~180M tokens/month baseline.
- Peak multiplier: planning for 2x on large campaigns (so ~360M tokens in peak month).
- Environments: we need 3 - prod, staging, and a shared sandbox for partners. Prod and staging must be isolated; sandbox can be lower performance.
- Budget range: internal guidance is between $100k- $300k ARR for infra + licensing this year; flexible if unit economics justify it. Our procurement lead is procurement@paymentsai.com (cc'd on future threads).

Target $/1M tokens: we'd like to land around $400- $600 per 1M tokens total (license + runtime equivalent) but willing to discuss structured deals (committed volume discounts, multi-year).

Happy to hop on a quick call with procurement next week.

Cheers,
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product - PaymentsAI
---

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>, procurement@paymentsai.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing discovery - next steps

Sanjay - thanks for the details, this is very helpful. Quick reaction and a proposed commercial construct so procurement has something concrete to review: 

Proposed commercial model (Private/VPC):
- Fixed annual platform license (on-prem/private control plane) - covers control plane, model packaging, and baseline support. Example range: $60k- $120k/year depending on support tier and SLA.
- Per-1M token tranche pricing for inference (metered at the Redwood side or reported by your usage agent) - tiered pricing with volume discounts. Example ballpark: $750/1M tokens at low volumes, stepping down to $350/1M at high committed volumes.
- Committed volume discounting: a 12-24 month commit can reduce effective $/1M to your $400- $600 range depending on environment count and support.

Support tiers (high level):
- Standard: business hours, 8x5 response, tech support via ticketing; included in base license.
- Enterprise: 24x7 coverage, designated TAM, runbook reviews, quarterly QBRs, and SLA credits - add-on 20-35% on top of license.

Environments: pricing model assumes 2 production-equivalent instances by default; additional isolated environments (sandbox) are cheaper but still carry resource reservation costs - each additional environment is typically priced as a % of the license (e.g., +15-25% per prod-like environment).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Ben to produce a draft pricing worksheet reflecting your 180M steady-state / 360M peak and 3 environments to show license + token-based cost ranges (I'll include a committed-volume scenario to hit ~$400/1M).
2) If procurement wants an SOW/quote, we'll prepare a redlined SOW + sample contract and a DocuSign-ready quote.

Marissa - can you and Michael take the token-cost example and produce the worksheet (estimates for standard vs enterprise support + 12/24 month commit)? I’ll queue procurement and send the DocuSign link once we finalize numbers.

Sanjay - does this high-level construct map to your commercial expectations? I can be flexible on license shape if you prefer an up-front credit against future token usage.

Thanks,
Ben
---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay@paymentsai.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Private/VPC pricing discovery - token cost examples attached

Adding the cost math and a few technical notes - see attached.

Highlights from the attached workbook (private-vpc-pricing-breakdown.xlsx):
- Baseline assumptions: 180M tokens/mo steady-state (~2.16B tokens/yr).
- Runtime unit economics: with our Dedicated/Private runtime and x16 quantization options, estimated effective cost to Redwood is ~$40- $90 per 1M tokens depending on model family and latency SLOs. 
- Commercial ranges: without a commit, list-ish pricing gives $700- $850/1M. With a 12-24 month commit for the volumes you shared, we can get to $350- $480/1M. For your stated target of $400- $600/1M, a 12-month commit + enterprise support (or a 24-month commit at standard support) lands inside that band.
- Environments: extra isolated environments add ~18% of base license per prod-like environment; sandbox counted at 5-8% given shared resource policies.

Attachments: private-vpc-pricing-breakdown.xlsx (XLSX, 220KB)

Notes: if low-latency (<100ms p95) is required for prod we may need a higher-cost kernel path which slightly increases the $/1M on peak traffic - I flagged those rows in the sheet.

I’ll update the workbook with the 3-environment scenario and send a DocuSign-friendly quote draft once Ben confirms which support tier you want to see priced.

-M
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
